name: Unexplained ₹12,000 salary deduction
expected: Explains Section 7 Payment of Wages Act 1936 limiting authorized deductions; arbitrary withholding is illegal.
prompt: My company deducted ₹12,000 from my monthly salary without any explanation or notice. Is this allowed?
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you navigate your employment issue safely and fairly.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee whose company has deducted ₹12,000 from your monthly salary without providing any prior notice or explanation. This arbitrary financial reduction creates an immediate dispute regarding your entitled earnings under Indian employment law.

### | Your Legal Position
* Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, your employer is legally obligated to pay your full wages on time without unauthorized delays.
* Under Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, employers can only make authorized deductions (such as provident fund contributions, income tax, or deductions for loss caused by your default, provided a proper inquiry was held). 
* Any arbitrary or unexplained deduction from your monthly salary without a formal inquiry or valid legal justification constitutes an unlawful deduction.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your employment contract, salary slips for the affected month and previous months, bank statements showing the credit amount, and any written communication or emails regarding the deduction.
2. Send a written demand notice to your employer's HR department or management requesting a formal explanation and full refund of the ₹12,000 deduction, granting them a period of 15 days to respond and settle the amount.
3. If the employer fails to refund the amount within the stipulated time, approach the jurisdictional Labour Commissioner or file an application under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 before the designated Authority for recovery of delayed or unlawfully deducted wages.

### Information I still need from you
1. What is the specific location (city and state) where your office is registered, and do you know how many employees work in your establishment?
2. Did you receive a formal payslip or any email communication explaining the deduction prior to your salary being credited?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.
